approved: Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2020

The Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2020 was moved, proposing a permanent ban on live animal exports for slaughter from 1 July 2023 with interim welfare safeguards. The speech cited specific incidents of animal cruelty, including 35,000 sheep shipped on the Al Kuwait in June 2020, breaches in Jordan, and inhumane slaughter in Indonesia, and criticised the government and opposition for blocking reforms.

The speaker seconded the Live Animal Export Prohibition (Ending Cruelty) Bill 2020, which would permanently ban live animal exports from 1 July 2023, and cited the Al Kuwait ship’s June departure despite a May heat ban and the Gulf Livestock I sinking that left 6,000 cattle and crew member Will Mainprize missing.
